'''Papora–Hoanya''', also known as '''Bupuran''', '''Hinapavosa''', '''Papola''', '''Papora–Hoanya''', '''Hoanya''' and '''Vupuran''', is an extinct [[Formosan languages|Formosan language]] of [[Taiwan]]. It was made up of the Papora and Hoanya dialects which were spoken across the middle western side of the island, ranging from [[Dajia District|Dajia]] to [[Dadu District, Taichung|Dadu]], and inland to [[Taichung]].<ref>[http://www.ethnologue.com/show_language.asp?code=ppu Ethnologue]</ref> The earliest found report of its extinction was from 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-03-04 |title=Ethnologue report for language code: ppu |url=http://archive.ethnologue.com/16/show_language.asp?code=ppu |access-date=2024-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304081441/http://archive.ethnologue.com/16/show_language.asp?code=ppu |archive-date=2016-03-04 }}</ref>

== Phonology ==
{{Cleanup section|reason=Convert into table|date=November 2024}}
Papora–Hoanya contained the [[consonant]] [[phoneme]]s [[Voiceless bilabial plosive|p]], [[Voiceless alveolar plosive|t]], [[Voiceless velar plosive|k]], [[Voiceless dental fricative|θ]], [[Voiceless alveolar fricative|s]], [[Voiced bilabial plosive|b]], [[Voiced dental and alveolar plosives|d]], [[Voiced dental, alveolar and postalveolar lateral approximants|l]], [[Voiced bilabial nasal|m]], and [[Voiced dental, alveolar and postalveolar nasals|n]] and others though it lacked the consonants [[Voiceless uvular plosive|q]] and [[Voiceless glottal fricative|h]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Shibata |first=Kye |date=2022-01-01 |title=Reexamining the historical relationships of the "Western Plains" languages |url=https://www.academia.edu/102433284 |journal=South East Asian Linguistics Society Annual Meeting}}</ref>
